newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MSCI may raise SingTel weighting - paper.
newsitem.headline: MSCI may raise SingTel weighting - paper.

text.p: The weighting of Singapore Telecom (SingTel) may rise in the benchmark Morgan Stanley Capital International's (MSCI) Singapore indices following a quarterly review, the Business Times (BT) said on Wednesday.
The local newspaper said the increased weighting would follow SingTel's placement and sale of more shares to the public earlier this year.

The report quoted Giacomo Fachinotti, managing editor of Capital International Perspectives SA, the Geneva-based statistics firm that calculates the indices, as saying the sale of the shares to the public was the type of move that "may drive a change" in an index when components are reviewed quarterly.
Quarterly adjustments to the indices will next be announced in the middle of November and will be effective two weeks later.
A higher weighting is expected to increase demand for the stock, particularly among index-linked funds, the BT said.
SingTel currently represents 18.7 percent of MSCI's Singapore Index.
Presently, only 40 percent of SingTel's total market capitalisation of Singapore $46 billion is included in the MSCI.
Morgan Stanley officials were not immediately available to comment on the report. -- Singapore newsroom (65 8703080)
